correctness.rationale: The proof was independently reconstructed. A \(k-1\)-dimensional hyperplane \(H\) of an LCD \(k\)-space has radical dimension at most one. If \(H\) is nondegenerate, LCD extensions correspond to vectors of norm one in \(H^\perp\), giving exactly \(2^{n-k}\); if \(\operatorname{rad}H=\langle r\rangle\), LCD extensions are exactly quotient cosets with \(B(r,x)=1\), again \(2^{n-k}\). For adjacent \(C,D\), every common neighbor either contains \(H=C\cap D\) or lies in \(W=C+D\), contributing \(2^{n-k}-2\) and \(2^k-2\). The unique possible overlap is the third \(k\)-subspace between \(H\) and \(W\); in characteristic two it is degenerate in both radical cases, so the sets are disjoint. Thus every edge has \(2^k+2^{n-k}-4\) common neighbors. Independent enumeration for all parameters through \(n=5\) reproduced every degree, lambda, and triangle count.

originality.rationale: The complete primary 2026 LCD-neighbor paper was read across all sections. It determines vertex degree, connectedness, and regularity/biregularity of orthogonal-orbit subgraphs, but it does not state a constant adjacent-common-neighbor number or a triangle formula. The same project's earlier public presentation explicitly listed triangle counting as ongoing work. Focused searches under LCD neighbor, nondegenerate subspace Grassmann graph, common neighbors, edge-regular, and the exact candidate formula found no prior theorem. The new star/top decomposition and binary degeneracy argument are not a routine substitution into the published degree formula.

The result is binary Euclidean only and does not determine nonadjacent common-neighbor parameters.

value.rationale: The source project explicitly identified triangle counting as an open structural task. The retained theorem answers it uniformly for every binary dimension and strengthens the global count to edge-regularity, a local invariant relevant to clique and classification questions. This is a motivated all-parameter structural lemma, not a routine small-parameter census.
